runs.content: Duke Energy rose 1.1% as utilities and staples were the only sectors up on a 1.9% AI-led S&P fall; Q3 EPS grew 10% with the 2026 guide narrowed to the top end, at ~18x forward earnings and a 3.4% yield, and it is the book's first utility; LOW was trimmed for capacity at −1.94% ahead of its 11-18 report.

Valero trades at ~7x forward earnings after a 19% pullback from its high and returns about half of its operating cash flow, entered on a day when energy was the only sector to rise; GPN was exited at −13.19% after its take-private talks reportedly collapsed.
